messages:
Sam: Customer forwarded 429s even though their project shows ~40% usage. They use one API key across multiple microservices behind a corporate NAT (~120 clients). Can we confirm why they're seeing 'remaining: 0'?
Priya: Can you paste a request_id and the X-RateLimit headers from one of the 429 responses?
Sam: Got one from the customer:
```
request_id: r-9b7c1
x-ratelimit-limit: 300
x-ratelimit-remaining: 0
x-ratelimit-reset: 2098765435
status: 429
```
Sam: Dashboard: project=~40% used, org=~85% used per their org view. They insist project shouldn't be hitting hard limits.
Marco: Two likely vectors: (1) IP-based affinity — if many clients share a single NAT'd IP we throttle the IP's burst and it looks like the API key is being punished; (2) org-level cap/fallback can preempt project-level allowance when org usage is high.
Priya: I pulled router logs for request_id r-9b7c1 — router shows policy applied: org_hard_cap. Snippet:
```
[ingest-07] policy=org_hard_cap applied (org=acme-corp) current=851/1000
[ingest-07] project=proj-88 usage=342/800
```
Helena: Billing note — acme-corp had a payment flagged earlier; our system auto-applied a conservative org cap (85%) while accounting was pending. That would cause org_hard_cap to trigger even if project still had headroom. @Sam can you confirm if the customer received any payment failure notices?
Sam: Customer says payment gateway shows 'pending' from yesterday, so billing hold might still be active.
Marco: For repro and root cause isolation:
1) From a staging machine, simulate ~120 clients using the same API key from a single egress IP (to mimic NAT).
2) Fire bursts: 10 rps sustained for 30s, watch x-ratelimit headers and router policy decisions.
3) Toggle the org-fallback feature_flag in staging (org_fallback=true/false) and repeat to see policy differences.
Priya: Extra edge-case: older SDKs (2.7.0 and earlier) have a quirk where usage attribution sometimes double-counts when the key is used across multiple project contexts; 2.7.1 includes a fix. If they're on 2.7.0 that could inflate org numbers.
Sam: They reported SDK version 2.7.0 in their app logs.
Marco: Action items: (a) Ops/Eng verify NAT aggregation behavior and whether IP-based burst accounting is too aggressive for shared NATs; (b) Eng confirm attribution bug in 2.7.0 and prepare backport if customer affected; (c) Billing confirm whether the hold can be cleared or temporarily relax the org cap while payment settles; (d) Support advise customer to rotate to project-scoped keys or split traffic across keys as short-term mitigation.
Helena: Opening billing ticket BL-5564 to request temporary cap lift contingent on confirming payment. Will update once processed.
Sam: I'll send the repro steps to the customer and ask for payment proof; will follow up here with request_id samples if they get more 429s. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
